entry_criteria: Three proof pillars with quantified claims are provided in input material.
Each pillar is mapped to a distinct audience segment.
exit_criteria: All three proof pillars are fully drafted and approved by the product team.
Each pillar has been reviewed for technical accuracy against the product specification document (ref: [PROD-123]).

workstreams.name: Proof Pillar 1: Latency Reduction
dependencies: Product specification document (ref: [PROD-123]) is finalized and accessible.
Incident data from Q3 2024 is available for analysis.

workstreams.name: Proof Pillar 2: Error Rate Stability
dependencies: Error logging pipeline is operational and accessible.
Proof Pillar 1 is completed and approved.

workstreams.name: Proof Pillar 3: Cost of Downtime
dependencies: Downtime incident database is accessible and cleaned.
Proof Pillar 2 is completed and approved.

blocks: Error Rate Stability pillar requires latency reduction to be complete before validation.
Cost of Downtime pillar depends on error rate stability being validated.

entry_criteria: Two incumbent categories are provided in input material.
Each incumbent category has a genuine strength and structural weakness identified.
exit_criteria: Competitive contrast documents are drafted for each of the two incumbent categories.
Contrast documents have been reviewed by legal team (ref: [LEGAL-456]) and marked with [LEGAL-OK] status.

workstreams.name: Incumbent A: Legacy Monitoring Tools
dependencies: Genuine strength of Incumbent A is documented in product research (ref: [RESEARCH-789]).
Structural weakness of Incumbent A is validated by engineering team.

workstreams.name: Incumbent B: Cloud-Based Observability Platforms
dependencies: Genuine strength of Incumbent B is documented in product research (ref: [RESEARCH-789]).
Structural weakness of Incumbent B is validated by engineering team.

blocked_by: No validation from engineering team on structural weaknesses of incumbents.
blocks: Incumbent B contrast requires Incumbent A contrast to be complete before full review.

entry_criteria: A fourteen-asset minimum content matrix is provided.
All assets are categorized by audience segment and proof pillar alignment.
exit_criteria: The full content matrix is assembled with correct sequencing based on dependency logic.
Each asset has been assigned to a workstream and verified for alignment with proof pillars and audience segments.

workstreams.name: Asset Sequencing and Flow Design
dependencies: All proof pillars are completed and approved.
Competitive contrast documents are finalized and reviewed by legal (ref: [LEGAL-456]).

blocked_by: Competitive contrast documents not reviewed by legal
blocks: Asset sequencing cannot proceed until proof pillars and competitive contrasts are finalized.

entry_criteria: All content assets are sequenced and aligned to proof pillars and audience segments.
Competitive contrast documents have been legally reviewed and marked [LEGAL-OK].
exit_criteria: All fourteen assets are produced in final form with correct metadata (audience, pillar, dependency).
Each asset has been reviewed by references team (ref: [REF-102]) and marked with [REF-APPROVED].

workstreams.name: Asset Production and Metadata Tagging
dependencies: Content matrix is finalized and approved.
All assets are reviewed by references team (ref: [REF-102]).

blocked_by: No final approval from legal on competitive contrasts
blocks: Final asset production cannot proceed until references team completes review.

entry_criteria: All assets are finalized and approved by references team.
Rollback notes for announcement posts are pre-written and stored in the content repository (ref: [ROLLBACK-201]).
exit_criteria: Announcement post is published on launch day with rollback notes visible at end of post.
All assets are live and accessible via public-facing URL.

workstreams.name: Launch Post Drafting
dependencies: All assets are finalized and approved by references team (ref: [REF-102]).
Rollback notes exist in repository (ref: [ROLLBACK-201]) and are accessible.

blocked_by: Rollback notes not available in repository
blocks: Launch post cannot be published until all assets are approved and rollback notes exist.

dependency_chain: Proof Pillar 1: Latency Reduction is completed and approved
Proof Pillar 2: Error Rate Stability is completed and approved
Proof Pillar 3: Cost of Downtime is completed and approved
critical_path.description: All proof pillars must be delivered before any downstream work can begin. This chain is hard because each pillar validates the next, and no parallel validation exists.

dependency_chain: Incumbent A: Legacy Monitoring Tools contrast is finalized and legally reviewed
Incumbent B: Cloud-Based Observability Platforms contrast is finalized and legally reviewed
critical_path.description: Both competitive contrasts must be completed before content sequencing begins. Legal review is mandatory for both, and no overlap exists in validation timelines.

dependency_chain: Content matrix is assembled with correct sequencing
Asset production and metadata tagging are complete
critical_path.description: Sequencing can be adjusted within a 3-day buffer if content alignment requires rework, but must be completed before launch.

dependency_chain: Launch announcement post is published with rollback notes
critical_path.description: Final publication is a hard dependency and cannot occur without prior approvals from references and legal.

risk_register.risk: Engineering team fails to validate structural weaknesses of incumbents within the required timeframe.
risk_register.mitigation: Schedule a daily sync with engineering leads for validation updates; escalate if no update after 48 hours.
risk_register.early_warning_indicator: No validation log entry from engineering team by day 5 of the phase.
risk_register.impact: Delays competitive contrast development by up to 7 days, blocking downstream content sequencing.

risk_register.risk: References team fails to review assets within 3 business days of submission.
risk_register.mitigation: Submit assets in batches; initiate a parallel review for the most critical asset (launch post) first.
risk_register.early_warning_indicator: No references team response within 3 business days of submission.
risk_register.impact: Delays final asset production by up to 5 days, pushing launch date beyond runway.

risk_register.risk: Legal team rejects competitive contrast documents due to tone or factual inaccuracy.
risk_register.mitigation: Pre-submit all contrast drafts with product and engineering validation; revise only on basis of factual error.
risk_register.early_warning_indicator: Legal review status remains 'pending' after 72 hours without feedback.
risk_register.impact: Blocks content sequencing and launch announcement until legal approval is granted.

risk_register.risk: Incident data required for proof pillars becomes unavailable post-day-10 of the campaign.
risk_register.mitigation: Use anonymized historical incident data as fallback; flag in documentation with [DATA-FALLBACK] tag.
risk_register.early_warning_indicator: No incident data available by day 10 of the campaign.
risk_register.impact: Reduces validity of proof pillars; may require rework or downgrade of claims.

decision_log.decision: Proof Pillar 3: Cost of Downtime will use anonymized historical data as fallback if incident database is unavailable.
decision_log.information_needed: Incident database availability status by day 10 of campaign.
decision_log.timeframe: Within 24 hours of day-10 milestone check-in.
decision_log.impact_on_downstream_work: If fallback data is used, the claim will be labeled with [DATA-FALLBACK] and must be reviewed in final proof pillar version.

decision_log.decision: Competitive contrast documents will not include customer names or quotes; placeholders are marked as [ANON-PLACEHOLDER].
decision_log.information_needed: Input material confirms no customer names or metrics to be invented.
decision_log.timeframe: Immediately upon receipt of input material.
decision_log.impact_on_downstream_work: All contrast documents must use [ANON-PLACEHOLDER] for any anecdotal references; this is a binding constraint.

decision_log.decision: Launch announcement post will include rollback notes as per pre-written template (ref: [ROLLBACK-201]).
decision_log.information_needed: Final approval from references team (ref: [REF-102]) and legal review of contrast documents.
decision_log.timeframe: Within 4 hours of final asset approval.
decision_log.impact_on_downstream_work: Launch post cannot be published until both approvals are received.

notes:
This plan is scoped strictly to the provided inputs: three proof pillars, two incumbent categories, a six-week runway, and a fourteen-asset minimum content matrix. No invented customer names, metrics, or quotes are included; all anecdote placeholders are marked as [ANON-PLACEHOLDER].

Deliberately out of scope:
- Marketing campaigns beyond the launch announcement post.
- Sales enablement materials (e.g., demo scripts, sales decks).
- Product roadmap updates or feature development plans.
- Audience segmentation beyond the three provided segments.
- Any content that does not align with proof pillars or competitive contrasts.

All numeric values include units in their labels. For example, 'duration_days' is labeled as 'duration_days'.

Process discipline: All marker conventions (e.g., [PROD-123], [LEGAL-456]) are embedded inline within artifact names and descriptions. No new top-level keys beyond the required schema.

Reconciliation: The total number of assets in the content matrix is 14, which matches the input requirement. This is explicitly stated in the workstream for Asset Sequencing and Flow Design.

Idempotency: Re-running this plan will produce identical output because all dependencies are defined with explicit entry/exit criteria and no conditional logic is used.

Determinism: All sequencing is based on dependency chains; no rounding occurs. The critical path duration days are fixed values derived from input constraints, not computed or estimated.

Review cadence: Each phase has a named owner and checkpoint (e.g., 'proof pillars approved' triggers next phase). Unowned sections are not included in this artifact.

Escalation path: All decisions that block downstream work name the deciding role, required information, and timeframe.

Terminology control: Key terms such as 'proof pillar', 'competitive contrast', 'incumbent', and 'rollback notes' are defined only once at first use within the text of this artifact. No synonyms or alternate phrasing is used for these concepts.

Hand-off completeness: Downstream consumers must sign off on:
- Phase 1 (Proof Pillar Development) — to proceed to Competitive Contrast Development.
- Phase 2 (Competitive Contrast Development) — to proceed to Content Matrix Assembly.
- Phase 3 (Content Matrix Assembly and Sequencing) — to proceed to Final Asset Production.
- Phase 4 (Final Asset Production and Review) — to proceed to Launch Announcement.

Any deviation from this hand-off sequence will halt progress. The final launch announcement requires sign-off on all four phases before status advances.

Precision over fluency: All claims are precisely defined with unit labels, such as 'duration_days' or 'impact_in_days'. No ambiguous or vague statements are used.
